artists.biography:
Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs, often shortened to Pigs x7, is a British rock band known for its intense, high-energy performances and unique blend of psych-rock, stoner metal, and noise rock. Formed in Newcastle in 2012, the band includes Matt Baty on vocals, Sam Grant on guitar, Adam Ian Sykes on guitar, John-Michael Hedley on bass, and Ewan Mackenzie on drums.

Pigs x7 quickly gained a reputation for their thrillingly relentless live shows that are as much of an endurance test as they are a psychedelic trip. The band's gritty, feedback-laden sound pays homage to the heaviest of rock and roll traditions while also pushing boundaries with their eclectic influences and sprawling compositions.

The band released their debut album, "Feed The Rats", in 2017 to critical acclaim. This was followed by "King of Cowards" in 2018 and "Viscerals" in 2020, each further cementing the band's unique place in the pantheon of heavy music. The success of their records and their incendiary live performances have seen Pigs x7 grow from a cult favorite to a force to be reckoned with on the global stage.

perplexity.description:
Viscerals is the third studio album by British stoner metal band Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs Pigs, released in April 2020 through Rocket Recordings. Recorded in October and November 2019 at Blank Studios in Newcastle upon Tyne, the album represents a continuation of the band's heavy, abrasive sound while maintaining their experimental approach to composition. The record spans 38 minutes across eight tracks, with three singles—"Reducer," "Rubbernecker," and "Hell's Teeth"—released in promotion of the album.

Musically, Viscerals blends multiple heavy genres into a cohesive whole, described as a "bludgeoning amalgamation of metal, punk, and experimental noise at its most brutal." Critics have identified elements of heavy metal, alternative metal, psychedelic rock, sludge metal, stoner rock, doom metal, and noise rock throughout the record. The album showcases the band's characteristic approach to songwriting, with tracks ranging from brief, punchy pieces like "Blood and Butter" (1:39) to sprawling compositions such as "Halloween Bolson" (9:00), demonstrating their versatility within the heavy music spectrum.

The album received significant critical recognition upon its release, with The Guardian naming Viscerals one of the twenty best albums of 2020 in their mid-year list. This accolade solidified the band's position as notable contributors to contemporary heavy music, following their earlier recognition as "top 40 newcomers" in 2018.
